observed.facings.png: Three panels at one scale. Each shows a roughly teardrop-shaped cloud of about 80–100 small dusty grey-brown bodies, large ones in the lower middle and smaller ones at the edges. South: each body is a rounded central lump with layered petal-like flaps fanned out to both sides, seen from the front. East: the same bodies seen side-on, flaps swept back like tilted fans, all heading right. North: bodies shown as domed humps with flared, skirt-like flap tiers, seen from behind, with no faces visible. Real alpha on a checkerboard.
observed.south.png: A cloud of grey bodies at full resolution. Each body has a central rounded head/thorax with a hint of a dark face, and two or three tiers of soft rounded lobes splayed sideways. The lobes are dull, have no pattern and look soft and painterly. Nothing is under the cloud.
observed.east.png: The same swarm in profile. Each body is a small wedge with stacked swept-back lobes trailing behind a blunt head pointing right. Up close the swept lobes read somewhat like a moth's or bird's wings in flight. The palette is dull grey throughout.
observed.north.png: The swarm from behind: domed backs on top of two or three flared tiers of lobes, no eyes or faces. At a glance the single bodies look a little like small grey mushroom caps or flower heads.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the candidate is a small grey speckled cluster about a third of a cell across, well below the human's knee and smaller than the human's head. At normal play (32 px/cell) it is a tiny grey speck next to the rat.

observed.facings.png: Three facings at one shared scale on a checkerboard. South is an almost perfect furry ball, with a small rodent face set in the upper-middle: tiny dark eyes, small rounded ears, a little pink nose and a large fan of fine white whiskers. Two small paws peek out at the bottom. East is a side profile of the same animal as a rounded loaf: lower and longer than south, with a short snout and long whiskers on the right, a small ear, a small eye and a tiny tail nub at the left. North shows the rear: a round back with two small ears visible at the top, a pale round tail tuft at lower centre, hind feet at the bottom, and no face. The coat is a dense grey-brown agouti fading to cream below, with fine painted fur strands. Real alpha, nothing baked under the body.
observed.south.png: Full-resolution south view: a near-spherical fuzzy body with the face as an inset patch. Small eyes, a dominant whisker spray wider than the face, a tiny nose and mouth, small ears that barely break the outline, two front paws at the base. Painterly fur texture with a soft dark edge and a clean cut-out. The round face with tiny eyes reads a little plush or cute.
observed.east.png: Full-resolution east view: a side profile of a round-backed, low-slung body, longer than it is tall, with no neck. The snout points right and carries a long whisker fan. A small ear, a small eye and a small tail nub at the rear. Feet are barely visible. Clean alpha.
observed.north.png: Full-resolution north view: the rear of a pear-shaped ball, with small ear rims at the top, a round pale tail puff at lower centre and hind feet at the base. No face or eyes. Fur is consistent with the other facings. Clean alpha.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the creature sits in one cell beside the vanilla human, roughly hip-high to the human: a small burrowing animal. At 32 px per cell it reads as a pale grey-cream blob beside the rat, smaller than the human and clearly distinct from the brown ground.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North shows the back, a tail puff and hind feet, with no eyes or face.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: All three are angled ground-level views, not overhead.

SAME_SIZE.seen: The 16% height spread comes from east being a lower, longer side profile of a round-loaf body; widths are comparable across facings. It reads as the body's shape in profile, not a scale jump, though east is slightly flatter than the sphere shown on south.

SAME_ANIMAL.seen: The same coat, ears, whiskers and tail nub appear on every facing; the tail sits at the rear on east and at centre on north, so it turns with the body. South is more spherical than the east profile, a mild shape mismatch.

ALIEN.seen: A stranger might say 'fat hamster' or 'pika' at first glance, but most departures are present (spherical body, merged fuzz mass, oversized whiskers, small eyes, pebble outline), so by the rule this does not fail. Still borderline.

OURS.seen: Not a vanilla or donor sprite; it is bespoke art matching the description.

ALPHA.seen: Clean cut-out on the checkerboard; no ground patch or shadow.

SCALE.seen: Roughly a quarter to a third of the human's height, a small burrow runner; fits drawSize 0.8 and the description.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px it is a distinct pale round blob against the brown ground; it reads, though as a small blob.

observed.facings.png: Three facings at one scale on a checkerboard. South: a stubby, steeply foreshortened cone of tan, root-like body. A blunt rounded head sits at the bottom with two small dark eyes, and the body tapers up and away into a wispy, frayed tail tip. East: a long horizontal serpentine body in side profile. It has bulbous knots along its length, a rounded blunt head on the right with one small dark eye, and a hair-thin frayed tail on the left. North: a vertical body seen from behind, made of stacked bulbous knots. The rounded far end is at the top and it tapers to a frayed root-tip tail at the bottom. No eyes or face are visible. The whole thing is covered in fine fibrous hairs, with no scales anywhere.
observed.south.png: Full-res south: a rounded blunt head toward the camera, with two faint eyes half-hidden in fibrous fuzz. Behind it the body rises in foreshortened knotted segments to a split, frayed tip. Tan and ochre with painterly fibre detail. Clean transparent background.
observed.east.png: Full-res east: a knobbly, unevenly thick, root-like body lying straight along the ground, slightly undulating rather than coiled. The head on the right is a rounded, slightly flattened bulb with a small dark eye and a faint mouth line. It is not wedge-shaped, but it reads as a head. Root hairs bristle from the whole surface. The tail end frays like a root tip. Clean alpha.
observed.north.png: Full-res north: rear view, the body receding away from the camera. There are four bulbous nodes, the topmost rounded (the far head end, seen from behind, with no eyes). It narrows downward into a stringy root-tip tail with hairlike rootlets. Clean alpha.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the creature lies as a thin, knotted brown line about 0.8 cells long beside the vanilla human, much smaller than the human. At 32 px/cell it becomes a thin brown squiggle, low in contrast against the soil-coloured ground.

SOUTH_FRONT.seen: South shows the blunt head facing the camera at the bottom with two eyes; the body recedes behind it.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North shows the body receding away from the camera, stacked knots tapering to a root-tip tail; no face or eyes.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: All three are angled game-camera views: south and north are foreshortened along the body, east is a profile. None is a flat top-down silhouette.

SAME_SIZE.seen: The 287% height spread is a pose effect of a long thin body: it lies horizontal on east and is foreshortened vertically on south and north. Body thickness and the size of the knots match across facings.

SAME_ANIMAL.seen: Same tan, fuzz-covered knotted body, blunt head and frayed root-tip tail on every facing.

SIGNATURE.seen: The defining read, a creature that passes for a root, is clear: knotted, root-hair-covered and tan, like a dug-up root.

ALIEN.seen: The silhouette is serpentine, but the knotted root body and root-hair fuzz with no scales do not read as an Earth snake at first glance.

DEPARTURES.seen: (1) Knobbly, uneven, root-like taper: present, with bulbous nodes on east and north. (2) Fine root-hair fuzz, no scales: present on all facings. (3) Head hard to tell from a root tip, no wedge viper head: mostly present. The head is a blunt rounded bulb, not a wedge, but small dark eyes on south and east still mark it as a head. (4) Pressed along a vertical tunnel wall, not coiled: partly present. It is stretched straight and uncoiled, but a ground sprite cannot show a wall.

STYLE.seen: Painterly fibre texture, realistic, with no cute face and no cel shading.

OURS.seen: Own bespoke root-creature art; no vanilla snake donor.

ALPHA.seen: Clean transparent backgrounds on all facings, with no ground patch or shadow.
